intro:
Beyond the exam. Unit 4 is not tested on the AP® Precalculus exam; it is here because many classes teach it and it leads into calculus.

Three views on one stage. Motion: a point moves along a parametric path while the graphs of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ run beside it; an interval shows the average rates of change of $x$ and $y$ and the displacement between the two points. Vectors: drag the tips of $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ and watch their sum, difference or a scalar multiple, with magnitudes and the dot product. Matrices: a $2 \times 2$ matrix moves the whole plane; the unit square becomes a parallelogram whose area is $|\det A|$ times as large, and $A^{-1}$ moves it back.
howItWorks:
• Parametric motion: the point at time $t$ is $(x(t), y(t))$. The arrows on the path show the direction of motion as $t$ increases. On $[t_1, t_2]$ the average rate of change of $x$ is $\frac{x(t_2) - x(t_1)}{t_2 - t_1}$, the same for $y$; their ratio is the slope $\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}$ of the segment between the two points.
  • Vectors add and scale entry by entry: $k\left\langle a, b \right\rangle + \left\langle c, d \right\rangle = \left\langle ka + c, kb + d \right\rangle$. The magnitude is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$. The dot product $\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2$ is 0 for perpendicular vectors, positive when the angle between them is less than $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
  • Matrices: $A$ sends $(1, 0)$ to its first column and $(0, 1)$ to its second, and every other point along with them. $\det A = ad - bc$; areas are multiplied by $|\det A|$, a negative determinant flips the plane over, and $\det A = 0$ squashes it onto a line, so $A$ has no inverse. Otherwise $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{\det A}\left[ \begin{matrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{matrix} \right]$.
  • The slider in Matrices moves the plane gradually from where it starts to its image, so you can watch every point travel.
  • Keyboard: the draggable points move one unit with the arrow keys; on the motion stage the arrow keys change $t$.
